title: Adversarial Machine Learning
weeklyTopics: Intriguing properties of neural networks; Explaining and harnessing adversarial examples
Adversarial examples in the physical world; Limitations of deep learning in adversarial settings
DeepFool; On the effectiveness of defensive distillation
Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Neural Networks
Towards Deep Learning Models Resistant to Adversarial Attacks; Obfuscated Gradients
Efficient Adversarial Training with Transferable Adversarial Examples; bypassing detection methods
Ensembles of weak defenses; Robust physical-world attacks on deep learning visual classification
Provable defenses via convex outer adversarial polytope; Robustness-accuracy trade-off
skills: bias and fairness in ml systems
workloadNotes: Seminar-style graduate special-topics course: no exams. Students present an attack paper and a defense paper (with reproduction of results) during the semester, plus a semester-long open-ended final project (50% of grade) with a 20-minute presentation and an 8-page paper-style report near the end of term.
prerequisitesText: Graduate standing or instructor permission; prior exposure to machine learning (e.g. EECS 445 or similar); comfortable coding in Python and working in a Linux terminal; familiarity with linear algebra, probability, statistics, and calculus.
